target.title: refactor(macos): lock and unify PortGuardian tunnel record persistence so concurrent app instances cannot lose orphan records
target.body:
Related: #100477

## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up hardening and cleanup of the PortGuardian orphan-tunnel work from #100489. The record store had a remaining bug class: `record()`/`removeRecord()` rewrote `port-guard.json` from one app instance's in-memory view, so concurrent instances (prod + dev on one machine — the exact scenario from #100477) silently dropped each other's records. A lost record is an unreapable orphan after a crash, which undermines the reaper the file exists to feed. There were also two overlapping kill helpers (both spawning `/bin/kill` subprocesses, one without exit confirmation), a fire-and-forget record write that could leave a just-spawned tunnel untracked, and assorted vestigial structure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The record store now has one canonical write path: every mutation is a read-merge-write of the shared file under an `flock` on a sidecar lock file (the kernel releases it if the holder dies; the sidecar is needed because atomic writes swap the json inode). Ownership is explicit — `ownRecords` holds only pids this process spawned; disk entries from other instances are reap-plan input, never adopted, which kills the resurrection hazard where one instance re-persisted records a sibling had deliberately removed. Removals are content-guarded (reap, `removeRecord`): a record is deleted only if the file still holds the exact record that was classified, so a sibling's fresh record on a recycled pid always survives. The two kill helpers collapsed into one `Darwin.kill`-based TERM→KILL helper with confirmed-exit semantics, which also upgrades the local-mode sweep kill (previously fire-and-forget signal delivery). `RemotePortTunnel` now awaits the record write before returning (no untracked-orphan window), shares one teardown path between `deinit` and `terminate()`, and drops a test-only overload. Vestigial single-element port loops in `sweep`/`diagnose` were flattened and the duplicate DEBUG extensions merged.

## User Impact

Multi-instance dev machines get reliable orphan reaping: tunnel records can no longer be lost to cross-instance clobbering, so every crashed instance's tunnel stays reapable. Local-mode port takeover now waits for the squatter to actually exit before the gateway starts. No user-visible surface changes.

## Evidence

- All 8 focused port-guardian tests pass, including the real-process integration test; the reap plan test now also pins the new drop semantics (dead-pid records reported as drops, shadowed stale disk records superseded rather than dropped).
- Full local suite `swift test --package-path apps/macos --parallel`: 639 tests in 113 suites, all passed.
- `swiftformat --lint` clean; Codex autoreview clean on the first pass ("patch is correct", no actionable findings).
- Diff shape: +156/−130 lines with the net growth being the file lock and single write path that replace the clobber-prone scattered writes.
